endpoints.interpretation: NF270 achieved high rejection of most PFAS in tertiary wastewater at 90% recovery: >92% for C >= 4 PFAAs, >98% for Gen-X, and 63-92% for ultrashort-chain PFAS; rejection values remained stable over 45 days despite permeability loss due to fouling/scaling.

The loose NF270 membrane was used as an initial step to reduce EfOM and selected inorganic ions that interfere with downstream PFAS adsorption by GAC and IX, thereby improving overall treatment-train PFAS removal performance.

endpoints.interpretation: Over 45 days, membrane permeability decreased (higher feed pressure, lower temperature-corrected specific flux), indicating inorganic scaling, biofouling, or EfOM fouling; PFAS rejection in batch tests did not change appreciably, suggesting fouling affected hydraulics more than rejection.

limitations.statement: Only one loose NF membrane type (Filmtec NF270) and one tertiary-treated wastewater matrix were evaluated, which limits generalization to other membrane types, tighter NF/RO, or different water qualities.

PFAS were periodically spiked into the NF feed for high-recovery batch tests, so the membrane was not continuously exposed to PFAS over the entire 45-day operation, which may limit understanding of long-term PFAS–membrane interactions.

Membrane fouling and scaling were inferred from permeability decline, but specific foulant composition and detailed energy or flux data were not reported in the supplied text, constraining quantitative assessment of hydraulic performance and energy needs.

comparability.reason: Sorption data quantify PFAS accumulation on specific materials within the CCMS but are not measured on a basis that is directly comparable to permeate rejection or energy use metrics; they are best used qualitatively to inform residuals management rather than to compare treatment performance between membranes.

endpoints.interpretation: Substantial PFAS sorption occurred to non-adsorbent treatment materials and the membrane. Adsorbed total PFAS mass was dominated by PFOS, with long-chain PFAS exhibiting preferential adsorption. On a mass-normalized basis, the 0.2 µm cartridge filter accumulated the most PFAS, the BW30 membrane and ion exchange (IX) softening resin had similar PFAS accumulation, and greensand accumulated the least. PFAS chain length was the dominant factor for sorption to the filter, membrane, and IX resin, whereas sorption to greensand was more influenced by PFAS functional group.

limitations.statement: Sorption metrics are based on methanol extraction and solid-phase analysis of selected treatment materials from a single pilot CCMS, which may not capture all irreversibly bound PFAS or be fully representative of other systems, materials, or operating histories.

Detailed PFAS speciation for each material (beyond PFOS and minor PFAS group) and corresponding aqueous-phase concentrations at the time of sampling are not fully available in the provided text, limiting precise mass-balance and fate assessment.

study_scale.value: Pilot-scale spiral-wound NF90 membrane system treating semiconductor fabrication wastewater and lab solution, operated in single-pass and semi-batch modes

treatment.value: Nanofiltration using a commercial Filmtec NF90 membrane operated as a spiral-wound module in a pilot system, in both single-pass and semi-batch (reject recirculated) configurations after pretreatment of fab wastewater with cation exchange and cartridge/membrane filtration

records.citation: Griffin, A.M.; Bellona, C.; Strathmann, T.J. Rejection of PFAS and priority co-contaminants in semiconductor fabrication wastewater by nanofiltration membranes. Water Research 262 (2024) 122111.

comparability.reason: Single-pass NF90 data for TPS and TMAH are generated in a controlled pilot configuration with specified flux, recovery, and pretreatment, enabling comparison of co-contaminant rejection under consistent hydraulic conditions and matrix, though extension to other fluxes, recoveries, or membranes requires caution.

endpoints.interpretation: Percent rejection of fab organic co-contaminants TPS and TMAH based on feed and permeate concentrations at fixed flux and recovery in single-pass pilot operation.

limitations.statement: Rejection of fab co-contaminants TPS and TMAH was assessed at a single flux (25 LMH) and one low single-pass recovery (15%) in pilot single-pass mode, which may not represent performance across the full range of practical operating conditions.

Comparison between lab solution and fab wastewater showed more effective treatment for fab wastewater, but the study used only one fab wastewater composition and particular pretreatment, limiting generalizability.

quantitative_findings.name: TPS rejection at higher effective recoveries (semi-batch)

quantitative_findings.name: TMAH rejection at higher effective recoveries (semi-batch)

residuals_byproducts.statement: Even at relatively modest single-pass recovery, TMAH exhibited only moderate rejection (≈57%), implying significant TMAH residual in permeate unless higher recoveries or additional treatment steps are applied, whereas TPS showed high rejection (>94%).

treatment.value: Single-pass nanofiltration using a Filmtec NF90 spiral-wound membrane module at 25 LMH and 15% recovery, following cation exchange and fine filtration pretreatment, to assess rejection of fab co-contaminants TPS and TMAH in both lab solution and fab wastewater feeds
